This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh. Stocks are tumbling this hour, erasing the post's
midterms gains. NPR's Scott Horsley reports all of the major market indices are down 2.8% to roughly
5%. The sell-off in stocks began in the tech sector, then rapidly spread to the broader market.
Investors were already having second thoughts about high-priced stocks tied to the artificial
intelligence boom. Those doubts were amplified on Tuesday when voters in many parts of the country
showed their opposition to data centers. Stocks initially rallied after the election. Investors
often welcomed divided government as a check on the excesses of both parties. But that early
enthusiasm quickly evaporated. Some investors shifted money into government bonds, which pushed
yields lower. The average rate on a 30-year mortgage dipped below 7.2%, although that's still
almost a full percentage point higher than this time last year. Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
Texas Republicans are reeling after losing statewide races up and down the ballot this week.
Members of the party say they are now trying to figure out where they go from here.
Here's NPR's Ashley Lopez. Artemio Muniz is the co-founder of the Texas Federation of Hispanic
Republicans. He says for the GOP to win some power back in the coming election cycles, leaders are
going to have to repair the party's relationship with Latino voters. Muniz says anti-immigrant
policies in the last decade have done serious damage with this big chunk of Texas' population.
Now Texas is at a crucial juncture. It's going to have to make up its mind.
And the good thing about Texas is that there are plenty of Republicans out there that understand
this. Since election night, some GOP leaders have said they believe the party didn't govern
far enough to the right, setting up a struggle on the party moving forward. Ashley Lopez, NPR News.
The midterms brought record wins for Democratic women in the House and historic firsts in governor's
races. And Pierre's Windsor Johnston reports those gains also widen the gap between the two parties
with fewer Republican women headed to Congress next year. At least 108 Democratic women will serve in
the next Congress, up from 95 today. For Republican women, the numbers are moving in the opposite
direction. 30 hold seats now, but only 17 have won so far, with some races still undecided.
All told, women will make up 28 percent of the House. Voters also broke barriers in
gubernatorial races. In Georgia, Keisha Lance Bottoms will become the nation's first black woman
governor. In Texas, Gina Inahosa will be the state's first Latina governor. And in New Mexico,
Deb Haaland's victory marks the first for a Native American female. They'll join a
record group of 17 women from both parties occupying governor's mansions next year.
Windsor Johnston, NPR News. Attorney General Todd Blanche confirms ahead of the Justice
Department Civil Rights Division. Harvey Dillon is out after 18 months in charge. This is NPR News.
A new report finds a record share of first-time homebuyers are paying with all cash. NPR's Jennifer
Ludden explains that a key to that is getting an inheritance. One in 10 first-time homebuyers pay
all cash, according to the National Association of Realtors, and more than a quarter of them use
inherited money. NAR deputy chief economist Jessica Lautz says they're also significantly
older than traditional first-time buyers, with a median age of 54. They waited a significant period
of time for that generational transfer of wealth to come through. Real estate agents say intense
competition and sky-high interest rates are driving all cash offers. And, of course, some
families don't wait until death to pass on money. The report notes it's all widening the divide
between homebuyers and those priced out. Jennifer Ludden, NPR News, Washington.
Cristiano Ronaldo is formally retired from international soccer. The Portuguese pro
footballer posted a lengthy farewell video today. He says the day has come for
me to hand back the number seven shirt of our national team. I never felt it belonged to me
alone. Ronaldo's career spans six World Cups. He played on the Portugal national team for
23 years and retires as the team's leading goal scorer. Comedian and media personality Russell
Brand has been convicted of rape and sexual assault in Britain. The judge told the 51-year-old today
that he faces a lengthy prison sentence. Sentencing is next week. Brand denies the charges.
